correctness.rationale: For a strictly convex body, slicing parallel to a fixed nonzero translation gives a strictly concave chord-width function on the orthogonal projection. A positive width level lies on the boundary of a convex superlevel set and is therefore null in the projection; local Lipschitz regularity of the endpoint graph then makes every nontrivial boundary-translate intersection surface-null. Surface measure consequently satisfies Ortega-Cerdà's general boundary criterion, whose remaining hypotheses hold for every convex body.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Ortega-Cerdà proves the corresponding theorem for bounded convex domains with C2 boundary and supplies the general boundary-measure criterion, but does not state the arbitrary strictly convex no-regularity theorem. Wan's simultaneous theorem covers different geometric classes. Exact and synonymous searches and the current SCOPE archive did not locate this strict-convexity extension. Recency leaves residual risk of unindexed simultaneous work.

value.rationale: The result removes all boundary differentiability from a newly established exponential Riesz-basis obstruction on a natural geometric class and identifies strict convexity itself as sufficient to force the required translate-nonoverlap.
